title: Changed conditions reveal agreement’s limit

captions.physics: Tying new conversation to earlier agreement

meaning: You can account for changed conditions while noticing how invoking earlier agreement binds a new answer and sharply reveals an unspecified limit.
text: On your Vishuddha, the Devil in the physical position can appear in tying a new exchange to earlier consent. The Wheel of Fortune in energy encourages accounting for actual changed circumstances and finding a suitable answer now. The Tower in emotions brings an abrupt experience of a broken assumption. You can want to preserve agreement and discover its conditions were understood differently. This distinction determines neither all closeness nor the next conversation’s outcome.

For example, you agreed to a personal call and later learn that another participant is proposed. “We already agreed” holds the new answer inside earlier consent. **A changed conversation needs actual confirmation**. You ask whether the new group suits. Discovering a boundary can startle more than the proposal itself. Yet the question does not declare the third person always unwelcome; a specific condition absent from the initial answer has changed.

Sharpness grows if restoring familiar certainty requires an immediate “yes”. A new condition then tests reliability and returns the earlier constraint. The constructive Wheel helps account for real change without an assigned conclusion. You can recognise surprise and hear readiness; agreeing to an earlier form does not guarantee acceptance of another, while a new request does not make the earlier agreement empty or originally insincere for you both.
